answer: Nonce-Chained Task Ledger. Each identity must submit a fresh, verifiably random sonnet-derived nonce with every action, hash-chained to its prior entry so replay fails. Duplicate or reused nonces are rejected, forcing attackers to generate and store unique work per identity. Costs include persistent per-identity state and continuous compute, while a ripple of failed submissions flags sybils. Cross-checks draw on karst-like sparse audit sampling, raising marginal cost sharply as fake identities multiply.
